scenes.say: Housing law changes by address, by building and by date. Ask an AI, and it may guess. Proofline answers with the law's own words.
Enter an address. Proofline finds the state and local rules that apply today, each with the exact quote, source and date.
Before a property manager raises the rent, check the change. Nine percent? Not allowed. The limit here is 1.6 percent, and here's the ordinance that proves it.
Proofline never turns missing data into a confident answer. If a fact is missing, it says exactly what it needs. Answer it, and every result updates.
When laws change, it shows which homes are affected and flags conflicts for human review.
scenes.callout: NJ FAIR Act: 140 homes affected, 90 conflict flags

scenes.say: Plain AI with search invented rules that don't exist. Proofline: zero, across 2,010 checks. It doesn't ask you to trust AI; it lets you verify every answer. Proofline, by Team USV.
I'm Ujwal, Team USV. Proofline isn't a chatbot: AI reads the law once, then a deterministic engine answers, and missing facts give 'unknown', never 'no'.

Claude turns each law into structured rules with a coverage test: Opus 5.5 for the corpus, Sonnet 5.5 for laws added live. Then code checks every quote word for word against the source: no quote, no rule. A second pass tries to disprove each one.
32 tests include checks from the organizers' own statements. Verify re-hashes the audit log, re-finds every quote, and reproduces all 500 addresses with zero differences.
scenes.callout: 32 tests passed  ·  verify: all checks PASS

scenes.say: The same model with search invented rules twice. Proofline: zero.
The AI reads the law; tested code answers users. That's why the same pipeline expands to a new city without rebuilding the product. We added Bayonne, New Jersey, live.
scenes.callout: API  ·  MCP  ·  CI  ·  Bayonne added live

scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ujwal, Team USV. I'm a software engineer working across backend systems, cloud infrastructure and AI applications. I built Proofline solo for the RealPage challenge.

What interested me was the trust problem. Housing law is exactly where an AI system shouldn't sound confident when it doesn't know. In Berkeley, 43 percent of rent-controlled tenants didn't even know they were covered.
scenes.callout: Berkeley: 43% of rent-controlled tenants did not know they were covered

scenes.say: In one weekend, Proofline turned 83 law documents into 74 verified rules for 500 homes in three states, with a rent change check, live law tracking, and an open API.

I built the whole system around evidence: verified quotes, deterministic decisions and explicit uncertainty. Every answer comes with its proof, so renters and housing providers can check it for themselves. Thanks for watching, and I would love your feedback.
